reviews.counterexample: An inscription has a true role and reader A records its groups correctly. Readers B and C make the same boundary error exactly at the informative loci. The true role fails the proposed cross-reading/intersection gate. No fact about its truth changed.
reviews.consequence: This gate can reject a reading-robust implementation, not the underlying semantic role. Three projections of one manuscript are not independent meaning witnesses. Neither sparse coverage nor a non-significant association is a semantic counterexample.
reviews.required_repair: Name one exact target and separate inscription hypothesis, error model, register restriction, support/power gate and robustness outcome before selection.

reviews.counterexample: A and B both realize semantic role R. A is licensed only in context C1, B only in C2 (a contextual realization rule); both contexts occur. Their frames are disjoint although R(A)=R(B). Even genuine context-free interchangeability can fail an observed reciprocal-transfer threshold by finite sampling.
reviews.consequence: Reciprocal observed frame equality is not necessary for a shared broad role. A tested violation can concern the stronger frozen interchangeability model; low power or absent observations remain inconclusive. Do not refute meaning by failure to outperform opaque controls.
reviews.required_repair: Distinguish semantic family, conditional realization, directional inclusion and context-free interchangeability; freeze target pair/context and uncertainty/capacity policy before selection.

limits: Abstract logical countermodels only, not Voynich observations or new experimental controls.
No runner, synthetic corpus or empirical test was needed to show the inference is overbroad.
Original raw proposal text remains unchanged; append-only reviews can mark method scope and missing design requirements.
